findings.reason: UNTRUSTED SOURCE: usbdev->config->interface[] is the actconfig interface-pointer array sized solely by the device-declared bNumInterfaces recomputed by usbcore from the raw descriptor stream a physically attacker-controlled USB gadget presents at enumeration (parser accepts configurations with fewer interfaces than the driver's device model assumes, warning only); a spoofed Wacom wireless-receiver gadget can present a configuration with only 1 or 2 interfaces. MISSING GUARANTEE: wacom_wireless_work (drivers/hid/wacom_sys.c:2437) indexes usbdev->config->interface[1] at line 2458 and interface[2] at line 2464 with hardcoded assumed indexes and never checks usbdev->config->desc.bNumInterfaces > 2 before either access; grep of wacom_sys.c returns ZERO bNumInterfaces occurrences (count=0), and these two lines are the only interface[] references in the driver. UNSAFE USE: the fetched pointers are immediately passed to usb_get_intfdata(), which is 'return dev_get_drvdata(&intf->dev);' (include/linux/usb.h:263-266) and therefore dereferences the interface pointer to reach its embedded device; the results are then chain-dereferenced at 2459-2461 (wacom1 = hid_get_drvdata(hdev1); wacom_wac1 = &(wacom1->wacom_wac); wacom_release_resources(wacom1)) and identically for interface[2] at 2464-2466. For an out-of-range slot (NULL or uninitialized) this is a NULL/wild-pointer dereference in workqueue context. TRIGGER: the work is scheduled from device-supplied HID data: wacom_wac.c:3245 and 3254 call wacom_schedule_work(wacom, WACOM_WORKER_WIRELESS) when the wireless status report changes the reported PID or disconnects, i.e. mere input from the plugged malicious device, after probe of the wireless-receiver interface (INIT_WORK at wacom_sys.c:2780). COUNTEREVIDENCE CHECKED: no bNumInterfaces validation anywhere in wacom_sys.c/wacom_wac.c; the same fixed-index shape was proven in sibling snapshots (facts f012, f018), and this snapshot's copy is unchanged. Same trust-boundary flaw as the seed cx231xx bug: an assumed index justified only by a device model, never validated against the descriptor-declared count. Impact is crash-class (local DoS from device plug-in plus one HID report); no write primitive claimed.

candidates.reason: wacom_wireless_work fixed-index usbdev->config->interface[1]/[2] (2458, 2464) with zero bNumInterfaces references in the whole file (grep count 0); usb_get_intfdata dereferences the fetched pointer (dev_get_drvdata(&intf->dev), include/linux/usb.h:263-266) and results are chain-dereferenced via hid_get_drvdata -> wacom_release_resources; scheduled by device-supplied wireless HID report (wacom_wac.c:3245/3254). Reported as the primary finding.

The fact-f002 intf_cache[0]->altsetting[1] pattern is FIXED in this snapshot: stv06xx_isoc_init reads intfc = actconfig->intf_cache[0] (line 316) and guards 'if (intfc->num_altsetting < 2) return -ENODEV;' (318) before alt = &intfc->altsetting[1] (321) and 'if (alt->desc.bNumEndpoints < 1) return -ENODEV;' (323) before the endpoint[0] write (326). stv06xx_isoc_nego re-indexes altsetting[1].endpoint[0] (343-345) but only after isoc_init validated existence (comment at 340-342); the gspca core invokes isoc_init before the nego retry path. Evidence-backed negative for this snapshot.

Same fix present: sd_isoc_init takes intfc = actconfig->intf_cache[0] (2648) and checks 'if (intfc->num_altsetting < 2) return -ENODEV;' (2650) then 'if (alt->desc.bNumEndpoints < 1) return -ENODEV;' (2655) before the endpoint[0] wMaxPacketSize write (2658); sd_isoc_nego's altsetting[1].endpoint[0] access (2684-2686) is preceded by the isoc_init validation per the code comment. Guards at 1445, 2650, 2655 confirmed by grep. Evidence-backed negative.

QDL path switches to altsetting[1] only under 'if (serial->interface->num_altsetting == 2)' (246); num_altsetting > 2 is rejected (248) and the ==1 case is handled separately (256). The altsetting index is validated against the descriptor-declared count before use — correct count-validated pattern.
'if (serial->interface->num_altsetting == 2)' guard precedes the altsetting switch; count validated before indexed use.

intf2 = dev->actconfig->interface[i] sits inside a loop bounded by dev->actconfig->desc.bNumInterfaces (the same descriptor-declared count that sized the array) with a NULL check on intf2 before use; identical to the safe pattern recorded in facts f003/f018 for sibling snapshots.

struct usb_interface *uif = udev->config->interface[i] is loop-bounded by the configuration's interface count (same descriptor-declared count that sized the array); no assumed fixed interface index in em28xx.

xusbatm_find_intf (45) and the unbind path (139) iterate i < usb_dev->actconfig->desc.bNumInterfaces, NULL-check actconfig->interface[i], and use usb_altnum_to_altsetting for the altsetting; altsetting numbers come from module params, not device data, and core usb_set_interface validates them.

'if (interface == dev->actconfig->interface[0])' at 347 is a pointer-identity comparison (a short array yields NULL, merely making the comparison false); line 351 dereferences actconfig->interface[0]->cur_altsetting only after establishing the probed interface IS interface[0], i.e. a non-NULL bound interface, and the endpoint loop is bNumEndpoints-bounded.

desc = &c->intf_cache[0]->altsetting->desc: intf_cache[0] is the first entry of a configuration usbcore accepted (a config parses with at least one interface cache) and '->altsetting' names the flex array's first element (altsetting[0]) of an interface cache with num_altsetting >= 1 by construction of the parser; neither index is an assumed multi-element index. Structurally in-bounds at the interface/altsetting level.

alts = &iface->altsetting[1] (also midi.c:2072, misc/ua101.c:905/1002/1010, mixer.c:3090, mixer_quirks.c:1659, quirks.c:235/453) assumes num_altsetting >= 2 with no local check; grep-enumerated in this finalize pass but not deep-read to their guarding format-table/altset construction (upstream, stream.c builds format entries only from enumerated altsettings, which would make the selected alt index count-derived). Left unresolved per the finalize instruction not to resume the full audit.

cdc_ncm/cdc MBIM runtime alt-switch paths (usb_set_interface on the data interface followed by reuse of endpoint state validated against the old altsetting) were not deep-read in this finalize pass; the file exists in s12 but its bind/alt-switch code was not examined before the budget closed.

limitations: No compilation, Kconfig check, or USB-gadget reproducer was run (read-only snapshot; builds would go under $TMPDIR only); the wacom finding rests on structural source evidence: exact line reads at wacom_sys.c:2458-2466, grep-proven zero bNumInterfaces occurrences, and the usb_get_intfdata/ dev_get_drvdata(&intf->dev) dereference chain.

wacom_wireless_work triggering requires a wireless-receiver model (WACOM_DEVICETYPE_WL_MONITOR path) and a spoofed gadget presenting a configuration with fewer than 3 interfaces plus one wireless HID status report; whether out-of-range config->interface[] slots are NULL or uninitialized depends on usbcore allocation details (kzalloc'd array of nintf parsed entries), so impact is asserted at crash-class level, not a demonstrated write primitive.

sound/usb fixed altsetting[1] consumers (implicit.c:95, midi.c:2072, ua101.c:905/1002/1010, mixer.c:3090, mixer_quirks.c:1659, quirks.c:235/453) and the cdc_ncm/cdc MBIM runtime alt-switch re-validation paths were grep-enumerated but not deep-read in this finalize pass; they remain unresolved and would need one targeted pass to confirm the format-table-derived guarantee.

usbvision is absent from snapshot s12 entirely (neither drivers/media/usb/usbvision nor drivers/staging/media/usbvision exists, verified by ls), so the fact-f003 usbvision model-table interface-index recheck is vacuously clean for this snapshot.

drivers/media/usb/cx231xx/cx231xx-cards.c actconfig->interface[idx] sites (1565/1603/1647/1838) are the seed demonstration family and excluded per intent; core usb files (hub.c, driver.c, message.c, devio.c, devices.c, usb.c) index interface[] inside bNumInterfaces-bounded loops or via interface[0] of an accepted/bound configuration and were classified safe at grep/structural level only, not line-verified individually.

V4L2 VIDIOC_S_ALT runtime handlers beyond the ones named in the intent were not individually audited; the gspca core (gspca.c) and em28xx set-alt paths checked here are count-validated, but other drivers' S_ALT handlers in s12 were not exhaustively swept before finalization.
No Git history or external CVE databases were consulted (not permitted); classification relies on this snapshot's source content only.
